groups.title: NSF project: Future Proofing for Age-Related Changing Cognitive Abilities Using Smart Objects as Assistive Technologies
bullets: Designed and developed a Gemini-powered AI assistant that draws inferences from Gmail and Google Calendar, shows the source of each inference, answers questions by text or voice, and follows plain-language rules users write about what it may infer; built a synthetic persona with mock email and calendar data and produced a demo video used as a design probe in co-design sessions where participants authored rules and boundaries for AI inferences.

Designed and developed the protocol for a 7-participant, 14-session co-design study with people living with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia; defined and co-created design cards in Figma as brainstorming probes, and conducted one-on-one remote sessions (Zoom, FigJam) moving from a shared leaving-home use case to each participant's own meaningful use case.

Applied reflexive thematic analysis: independently coded and memoed 8 of 14 session transcripts, then collaborated with the research team to refine and finalize themes, testing counterexamples and verifying quotes against transcripts.

Conducted semi-structured interviews with people living with MCI or dementia about everyday technology use (three interviews per participant around a two-week diary study), adapting follow-up probes to each participant and building the post-diary interview on their own entries.

Proposed an adaptive systems framework of four user-configurable modules (sensing, inference, assistance authority, output delivery) and designed and developed the Adaptive AI Assistant that implements it: a Raspberry Pi leaving-home reminder system integrating Gemini, dlib face recognition, Google Calendar, and weather data, with a Flask web app where each user selects their level for every module (lead-author CSCW 2026 poster).

groups.title: Research assistantship
bullets: Analyzed older adults' self-presentation on TikTok, combining engagement data for 15,000+ videos from 23 creators with a team-coded set of 1,227 videos from 11 creators.
Mentored four undergraduate and graduate students across research and prototyping projects, from study procedures and qualitative analysis to building working prototypes.
Publications: lead-author poster, CSCW 2026; co-author, ASSETS 2026 full paper (Honorable Mention Award).

summary: Built and shipped web features for an early-stage startup, working with it through an Arizona State University program.
bullets: Turned Figma designs into responsive web applications in React and TypeScript, iterating with the design team from handoff to release.
Designed and integrated RESTful APIs to move data between user-facing features and the backend.
Built a HubSpot chatbot that automated customer engagement, cutting manual intervention by 40%.
Standardized 550+ templates with global variables, so one change updates everywhere and manual updates dropped by 80%.

summary: Radar perception and object tracking for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), the technology behind features like adaptive cruise control.
bullets: Implemented C++ multi-object tracking with a Kalman Filter, Interacting Multiple Model (IMM), and Probabilistic Data Association Filter (PDAF), improving vehicle tracking accuracy by 10%.
Improved ADAS object classification by 5% through MATLAB-based feature extraction and radar data analysis.
Identified and resolved a critical bug in which a truck was classified as two separate cars, raising classification accuracy by 15% and earning recognition from the Head of Group.
Labeled and validated 5,000+ video frames against radar sensor outputs.
